description:
FILED s510 (Fable, 2026-10-06) after brian d foy\x27s reply on r/perl ("how do you know rand takes one argument? I can redefine it" -- his blog post "Get real random numbers from Perl\x27s rand()" replaces rand and adds a list context).  Probes ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s510/review/foy/*.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main b06f833a-era.

WHAT IS RIGHT TODAY (ir-spec 7.1a, #1870/#1992): the replacement IS called for `use subs`, a `use M qw(NAME)` import list, `BEGIN { *CORE::GLOBAL::NAME = sub {...} }` and `BEGIN { package Other; *main::NAME = sub {...} }`; a plain `sub rand {...}` does not displace the built-in (b-plain-sub.pl, as perl); `use Time::HiRes qw(time sleep)` works (f-hires.pl); a replacement WITH a prototype is parsed by it (`use subs "length"; sub length (\@)` -- g-proto-override.pl); his own usage `my @a = rand(100)` with a list-context replacement works (i-wantarray.pl row 1).

THREE GAPS, all silent:
 1. THE PARSE (a-subs.pl, d-core-global.pl, e-glob-begin.pl, h-later-def.pl): `$, = "|"; print rand 5, sin 4, rand sin 1, 2, 3;` with a prototype-LESS replacement
      perl: myrand(5,-0.756802495307928,myrand(0.841470984807897,2,3))        (a user sub without a prototype is a LIST operator)
      PCL : myrand(5)|-0.756802495307928|myrand(0.841470984807897)|2|3        (the built-in\x27s named-unary rule is kept)
    With parentheses the two agree, which is how a stand-in for a built-in is normally called -- so the exposure is a paren-less call followed by more list items.  The fix belongs where the term rule is chosen: once `builtin_override_target` answers for a name, the argument rule is the REPLACEMENT\x27s prototype (none = list operator), not Config\x27s entry for the built-in.  CORE::GLOBAL: perl parses by the override\x27s prototype too (probe before assuming).
 2. A DEFAULT-EXPORT override (c-import.pl): `use MyRand;` where MyRand.pm has `our @EXPORT = qw(rand)` -- perl calls MyRand::rand, PCL calls the BUILT-IN.  The override is decided from the `use` statement\x27s own import list; a `use` with NO list takes the module\x27s @EXPORT, which PCL already reads for prototypes.  docs/not-supported.md lists only the `BEGIN { M->import }` spelling (#2053); this one is not written down.
 3. CONTEXT for a CORE::GLOBAL replacement (i-wantarray.pl): `my $x = rand(1)` inside a sub called in list context -- the replacement\x27s `wantarray` is UNDEF (void) where perl says scalar (false but defined).  The `use subs` spelling is right (j-subs-wantarray.pl: an ordinary sub call with its context bind).  So the CORE::GLOBAL route reaches the user code without a scalar bind.

LINK to #2775 (the list-context bind around built-ins): a REPLACED built-in is user code that reads `wantarray`.  In a LIST slot it gets list context today only through that fallback bind -- the analysis job must cover overridden built-ins before the bind is removed (added to its brief, section B).

SIZE: not scheduled.  Gap 1 is the one foy\x27s example hits; 2 is a plausible real import (a module that exports a drop-in `rand` / `sleep` / `time` by default); 3 is a corner.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, residue of the builtin-override work #1870): a REPLACED built-in is still PARSED with the built-in\x27s argument rule -- `use subs "rand"; sub rand {...}  print rand 5, sin 4, 2` gives the replacement ONE argument (perl: all of them, it is a list operator); plus a DEFAULT-export override is not seen, and a CORE::GLOBAL replacement reads `wantarray` wrongly in a scalar slot
